## Body

Copilot restarts are siblings, not a parent-child chain: the original CLI supervises each fresh restart, and the previous child exits. #263 passed source/CI review but failed live on restart 2. Its "second restart" fixture rebuilt the row with the original proc instead of feeding the first registration's returned descriptor forward. For external-process sequence tests, copy the observed process tree, advance the complete returned state, and make the previous incarnation absent. A repeated helper call is not a stateful sequence.

#265 keeps the original verified pid+proc_start in cache_proxy.anchor and copies it unchanged across sibling restarts. Match the exact anchor against daemon-observed ancestry, never the last child's proc alone. Clearing/replacing the whole route on non-descendant registration, gate failure, opt-out or revive must discard the anchor too; SQLite replaces the JSON column, not individual members. The repaired test feeds three successive descriptors forward, with only supervisor and current child alive.

Compatibility boundary: old gate stamps without anchor bootstrap from their verified row.proc. Already-carried #263 rows without anchor cannot recover the original supervisor because row.proc is r1; their next sibling may read plain. pm-001 explicitly accepted this under forward-only F221 (display only, heals on revive), not an owed backfill.

Reviewer pass-with-notes was reissued at rebased head 6b6419caadafa5b0926c8df92550ce39dc6116ff, output commit 7cbf87359f86eccd65555813559f6f9f82a92b24. The regression is the encoded lesson (D-F213-2); source/CI approval is not the post-deploy multi-restart proof.
